verdict_note: From reading only: no build and no tests were run. Both R60-a3 defects are closed as built. e1: RecipeTargets::write asks its port (doc_export.rs:1065) before run.checkpoint and the temp (:1085-1087), so no file byte reaches the destination before the ask. e2: the runner's Slot is released before TargetExporter::write (batch.rs:1096-1100) and asked again only before a native target (:1062-1067), so one port bound in both places never needs two slots. Settle-once holds by type: settle and complete take self, and Drop settles Abandoned. Slot accounting is balanced on every path. Folder removal cannot lose data: only folders for which create_dir returned Ok are named, and remove_dir never removes a non-empty folder or follows a link. One medium defect (F1, latent: no in-tree caller binds BatchPorts.jobs). The lend is unconditional. An exporter that does not ask the runner's own port, for example RecipeTargets without with_job_port, therefore runs its whole export with no slot on the host port; at base the runner's ticket covered it. The target job is also charged 0 bytes where the lent slot carried the input's bytes. F2 to F5 are low: the re-ask fails a native target non-retryably under contention; a mid-input cancel reaches both new asks and settles as failed; the compile_fail proof is weaker than claimed on the pinned stable toolchain; and no test covers the data-loss guard or the failed settlement.

findings.what: At c8fca900 the runner's Edit ticket on BatchPorts.jobs was held across every target, exporter writes included. Now it is released before every TargetExporter::write, whether or not the exporter will ask that port. With BatchPorts.jobs set to the host port and RecipeTargets::new(..) without with_job_port, the target asks a fresh asset-local port (16 slots) inside its throwaway viewer. The checkpoint, render, encode and write of every exporter target then run with no slot on the host port. Even with one shared port, the lent slot (bytes = input size) is replaced by a target job of 0 bytes. A byte-budgeted port is then charged nothing for the export's working set, which at base was covered by the runner's ticket.
findings.scenario: A one-slot port P bound only as BatchPorts.jobs, RecipeTargets::new(ctx) with no port, and one input with one png target. P is asked once (the runner) and is free from the lend until the input ends, so another P.admit made during the PNG write is admitted: two jobs run under a one-slot port. At c8fca900 the same ask during the write is refused.
findings.fix: Lend only to an exporter that will ask the runner's own port. The smallest shape: hand the runner's port to the exporter (a TargetExporter::write parameter, or set once in run_batch), and have RecipeTargets use it when with_job_port is unset. Otherwise keep the slot held (no lend) for an exporter that admits elsewhere. Also charge the target's export job with the input bytes or the checkpoint length (request(Action::Export, bytes, ..)), so the bytes of the lent slot stay charged.
findings.test: In tests/fix_export_admission.rs, a TargetExporter wrapper over RecipeTargets that records P's held count at write entry. With BatchPorts.jobs = P and RecipeTargets without a port, the export must run under a slot of P (held 1 at write, or P asked by the target). Also a byte-counting port asserting that the target's job carries the input's bytes.

findings.certainty: READ; not run. The re-ask itself is the lead-approved design; this is about how its refusal is handled.
findings.severity: low (a new failure mode under contention, absent at base; the receipt code invites a retry the runner never makes)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-harness-core/src/batch.rs:1062-1067 (a refused re-hold fails the native target), :1019 (an output-stage failure is retryable false), :816-818 (only before_output failures retry); crates/hsk-studio-harness/tests/fix_export_admission.rs:277-296 (pins the failure)
findings.what: Lending exists so that other work can take the slot during the export. So the busier the port, the likelier the re-ask before a following native target is refused. That refusal is a non-retryable output failure with code job_admission_refused(retry_after_ms=N). The input fails under SkipAndContinue, while the input's earlier targets are already written. A caller who honours retry_after_ms and re-runs the input gets duplicates under Rename (in-1.png). At base a native target could not fail admission mid-input.
findings.scenario: Targets [png, handshake] on a host port shared with another worker that takes the freed slot during the PNG export. The PNG is written, and the .handshake target fails with job_admission_refused(retry_after_ms=5) and no retry.
findings.fix: Remove the re-ask: write an input's native targets first under the held slot, then lend once for its exporter targets, keeping the receipts in job order. A native target and an exporter target cannot collide on a name, because DocFormat::extension is png, jpeg, tiff or psd and never handshake. Asks become 1 plus the exporter targets (native-png-native: 2). Alternative: one bounded, cancel-checked wait of retry_after_ms before refusing.
findings.test: native-png-native on a port that refuses every second ask while a slot is free: all three targets are written, and the receipts are in job order.

findings.what: Take a batch canceled while an input with exporter targets is running. The target's admission checks the export viewer's own token, so the bound port is asked and a ticket taken. Next, run.checkpoint() fails on the batch token, now after the ask. The job settles failed with batch_checkpoint_failed, not canceled, and the input is reported failed, not cancelled. The Canceled arm cannot be reached from a batch cancel. Slot::hold likewise asks the host port again after a cancel; the session lifecycle refuses canceled before asking (jobs.rs admit_within), the runner does not. At base the checkpoint ran before the target's ask, so a cancel never reached the bound port from a target.
findings.scenario: One port as runner and exporter port whose release() sets the batch token (the lend releases). Targets [png]: the port is asked twice, the target's ticket is taken and released, the receipt is batch_checkpoint_failed, and the input outcome is failed instead of cancelled.
findings.fix: Check the run's cancel before the target's ask and inside Slot::hold, and refuse 'canceled' without asking. Give the export viewer the batch's token, which needs RecipeTargets or TargetExporter::write to receive it, since Run exposes no accessor. Map a failed checkpoint through the run's last op error (as batch.rs last_error does), so that canceled settles Canceled.
findings.test: The scenario above: one ask, a target receipt of canceled, and an input outcome of cancelled.

answers.folder_removal: No data-loss path found. Non-empty: remove_made uses std::fs::remove_dir only. On Windows that is RemoveDirectoryW (read in the local toolchain's std sys/fs/windows.rs:1392-1395, 1.91.1; the pinned 1.97.1 source was not read), and rmdir on Unix. Both refuse a non-empty directory and never recurse, and the loop stops at the first folder that stays. Pre-existing: only a path for which create_dir returned Ok enters `made` (batch.rs:1128-1131). AlreadyExists, from an existing folder or one made concurrently after the is_dir scan, is skipped. An existing folder that cannot be statted (is_dir false) fails create_dir before anything is made. Links: an ancestor that is a symlink or junction resolving to a directory counts as existing, because is_dir follows links, and is never claimed. A dangling link or a file at a missing path gives AlreadyExists with !is_dir, which is Err with nothing made. remove_dir does not follow: rmdir on a symlink fails, and RemoveDirectoryW on a reparse point removes the link, not its target (Win32 documentation, not re-read here). Residual races, none of which loses content: (1) another process that adopted a folder this run just made, before writing into it, sees it vanish when this target is refused, and its write fails; (2) if our new folder is replaced by an empty folder or a link, or a pre-existing ancestor link is retargeted, between create and remove, remove_dir removes that empty folder or that link. Only exporter-target failures remove folders; a native failure keeps them (lane cut). A transient remove failure on Windows (sharing violation or delete pending) leaves empty parents behind, which is cosmetic.
answers.bytes_before_admission: No file byte. RecipeTargets::write does only these things before its ask: recipe lookup, run.snapshot, DomainId::parse, Viewer::with_context and set_job_port (doc_export.rs:1056-1065). The checkpoint, the temp, the open and the export all come after (:1084-1093). In the full batch, the runner creates the destination folder and its missing parents before an exporter target's ask (batch.rs:1069 runs before :1099). This is the lead's approved design, and a refused target removes those folders while they are empty. The made-folder test (:202-216) runs with the folder already present at the ask; it asserts the ask count only. A native target's re-ask comes before make_folders (:1062-1069). Not examined: run.stage_tile in process() before the runner's first ask (pre-existing, not the destination).
answers.settle_once: Holds by type. AdmittedJob::settle and complete take self (session jobs.rs:489-505). Ok goes to complete(head), and Err settles once (doc_export.rs:1066-1078). An admission refusal holds no ticket. A panic between the ask and the settle drops the job, and Drop settles Abandoned once (jobs.rs:552-557). Gaps: the Canceled arm cannot be reached from a batch cancel (F3). A panic inside write_admitted_target skips remove_file(temp), leaving the whole-document temp in the destination; this is pre-existing, and a guard type would fix it.
answers.slot_accounting: Balanced on every path. hold asks only when no ticket is held, lend releases only when one is held, and Drop lends (batch.rs:785-806). After a refused re-ask the ticket is None, so a later exporter lend is a no-op and the drop releases nothing extra. A retry attempt builds a new Slot, and the old one is dropped. Counts match the lane's: e2 is 2 asks and 2 releases; native-png-native is 3 asks and 3 releases; a refused re-ask is 3 asks and 2 releases. One port never has two slots held for one input, provided the exporter asks that same port. Gaps: F1 (no slot on the runner's port while an exporter that admits elsewhere runs, and a 0-byte charge), F2 (a refused re-ask fails the native target for good), F3 (both asks are made after a cancel).
answers.compile_fail: Weaker than claimed (F4). It shows that the snippet does not compile from outside the crate. On stable that holds for any reason, and in no case does it distinguish pub(crate). Module privacy is true on reading (no visibility modifier; the only callers are doc_export.rs:1065 and :1091).
answers.tests_vs_implementation: Both probes are ported faithfully and made stronger: probe e1 asserted only that every listing was empty, while the port asserts exactly one ask with the folder empty. The red tests are unchanged by later commits. Ask counts and the job_admission_refused string are pinned exactly; these are implementation pins, but each matches a count the lead approved. The gaps are in F5: the data-loss guard, the failed settlement, and the runner-port-only and cancel cases.

Q4 (F4): accept the typestate shape (the no-ask export takes the AdmittedJob) in place of a privacy proof by compile_fail alone?
